healthy.summary: Leaf tissue shows uniform healthy chlorophyll levels with minimal chlorosis or necrotic lesions.
immediate_actions: Continue routine scouting once a week on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Maintain balanced irrigation and avoid waterlogging around the root zone.
chemical_remedies: No chemical spray required at this stage.
organic_remedies: Optional preventive spray of Neem Oil (1500 ppm) @ 2 ml/liter every 15 days during high-pest season.
prevention_tips: Follow crop rotation and use certified disease-free seeds.
Keep field bunds free of weeds that harbor sucking pests.

blight.summary: Fungal or oomycete blight causing dark water-soaked necrotic patches and progressive foliage dieback.
immediate_actions: Remove and destroy severely infected lower leaves away from the field.
Stop overhead sprinkler irrigation immediately to reduce leaf wetness.
chemical_remedies: Preventive/Early: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/liter water (500 g/acre).
Curative: Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/liter OR Azoxystrobin + Tebuconazole @ 1.5 ml/liter.
organic_remedies: Spray Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/liter or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/liter during early stages.
Copper-based Bordeaux mixture (1%) for organic orchards.
prevention_tips: Maintain recommended plant spacing for airflow.
Treat seeds with Trichoderma (4 g/kg) or Carbendazim (2 g/kg) before sowing.

rust.summary: Rust fungus producing orange, yellow, or reddish-brown powdery pustules that reduce photosynthesis and grain filling.
immediate_actions: Inspect adjacent plots immediately as rust spores spread rapidly via wind.
Apply a systemic triazole fungicide within 48 hours of detection.
chemical_remedies: Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 ml/liter water; repeat after 15 days if humid.
organic_remedies: Wettable Sulphur 80% WP @ 2.5 g/liter (avoid spraying above 32°C).
Neem seed kernel extract (5%) as supplementary preventive.
prevention_tips: Grow rust-resistant varieties recommended by ICAR/State Agricultural University.

leaf_spot.summary: Fungal or bacterial leaf spots characterized by circular brown/black lesions often surrounded by yellow halos.
immediate_actions: Prune heavily spotted leaves and avoid working in the field when foliage is wet.
Improve drainage and apply targeted protectant spray.
chemical_remedies: Fungal spot: Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP @ 2 g/liter water.
Bacterial spot: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/liter + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/liter.
organic_remedies: Neem oil (3 ml/liter) + mild soap emulsifier.
prevention_tips: Use drip irrigation instead of flood/overhead watering.
Deep summer ploughing to bury infected crop residue.

mosaic_virus.summary: Viral infection causing yellow-green mottling, chlorosis, curling, and stunted growth; spread by whiteflies or aphids.
immediate_actions: Rogue out (uproot and bury) severely infected plants early to stop field-wide spread.
chemical_remedies: No direct chemical cure for plant viruses — target vectors with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/liter or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.5 g/liter.
organic_remedies: Install 8-10 yellow sticky traps per acre.
Spray Neem oil (1500 ppm) @ 3 ml/liter or Verticillium lecanii @ 5 g/liter.

powdery_mildew.summary: White powdery fungal coating on upper leaf surfaces and stems, thriving in warm days and cool dry nights.
immediate_actions: Ensure good canopy ventilation and avoid excessive nitrogen.
Spray sulphur or systemic fungicide at first sign of white patches.
chemical_remedies: Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1.5 ml/liter OR Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1 g/liter.
organic_remedies: Potassium bicarbonate (5 g/liter) or diluted buttermilk/milk spray (1:9 ratio) in early stages.
